best.plan_strategy: Final attempt: return to hist_gbdt — the single best-ranking generator this run has measured (roc_auc 0.9912, balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut 0.9585) — but at a materially different point in its capacity space than iteration 1 and with a class_weight nudge no hist_gbdt attempt has carried. Concretely: learning_rate 0.03, max_iter 900, max_leaf_nodes 15, min_samples_leaf 10, l2_regularization 0.5, max_depth 6, early_stopping false so all 2,760 training rows are used, class_weight {0:1, 1:1.2}. Pipeline: median impute, no scaling, no missingness columns — identical to iterations 1-3 so the only moving parts versus iteration 1 are the capacity settings and the weight, and no preprocessing lever confounds the read. Iteration 1 was the same family at 400 iters / lr 0.06 / 31 leaves and memorised the training split (train_balanced_accuracy 0.9995, gap 0.0461); many more, smaller, shallower, more strongly-shrunk and l2-regularised trees is the lower-variance point in the same space that trades that memorisation for a better-ordered validation ranking, which is the only axis with room left. The weight 1.2 sits just above the recall/specificity crossing that iteration 3 located at 1.35 on a differently-calibrated forest, and hist_gbdt's own cut at iteration 1 was specificity-biased (recall 0.9337 vs specificity 0.9731), so a mild push toward the positive class collects the ~0.005 the operating point still holds for this family. I will read roc_auc and balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut against 0.9912/0.9585 to see whether the ranking moved, and recall-vs-specificity plus cut_headroom to see whether 1.2 landed the cut near its optimum.

critic.evidence: Iteration 1 (hist_gbdt, 400 iters, lr 0.06, 31 leaves) scored balanced_accuracy 0.9534 on val against the 0.9614 bar — 0.0080 short — with 95% CI 0.9384~0.9671, which contains the bar, so the shortfall itself is not resolved by this slice (width 0.0287). No error type, train_time 4.46 s of a 600 s budget, no dropped_hyperparams, so neither oom, too_slow nor a dropped setting. The family is clearly right on the ranking axis: roc_auc 0.9912, pr_auc 0.9883, balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut 0.9585. The operating point is nearly exhausted — cut_headroom 0.0051 against 0.0080 still to go (64% at most), and recall 0.9337 vs specificity 0.9731 says the cut is only mildly biased toward specificity, so class_weight can buy at most that 0.0051 and the residual 0.0029 has to come from the ranking. What is diagnosable is capacity: train_balanced_accuracy 0.9995 vs val 0.9534, train_val_gap 0.0461 on 2,760 rows / 57 features — 400 unstopped iterations at lr 0.06 with 31 leaves has memorised the training split, so the settings, not the family, are what is off (one family tried, so wrong_model_family is not yet supported).
critic.direction: Stay on the ranking axis but keep it a single-lever move: refit hist_gbdt with the same preprocessing and a lower-variance capacity setting (learning_rate 0.03, max_iter 800, max_leaf_nodes 15, min_samples_leaf 10, l2_regularization 0.5) so the near-perfect train fit (train_balanced_accuracy 0.9995, gap 0.0461) is traded for a better-ordered validation ranking, which is where 36% of the remaining 0.0080 sits since cut_headroom is only 0.0051.

critic.evidence: Iteration 2 (xgboost, 900 trees, lr 0.03, depth 4, subsample 0.8, reg_lambda 3.0) scored balanced_accuracy 0.9517 vs the 0.9614 bar — 0.0097 short — with 95% CI 0.9358~0.9660, which contains both the bar and iteration 1's 0.9534; the paired Δ vs iteration 1 is -0.0017 (CI -0.0113~+0.0070, P(better) 0.352), so this slice does not resolve the two attempts and the move is not a regression, just unresolved movement. Note also that the row is not my prescription: I asked for a retuned hist_gbdt and the Planner ran xgboost, so the overfitting fix I prescribed was only partially delivered — yet the capacity lever did do what I said it would (train_balanced_accuracy fell 0.9995→0.9880, train_val_gap 0.0461→0.0363) and validation did not move outside the interval. That is the difference from last time: the gap is now unremarkable (0.0363 with train 0.9880, no memorisation left to trade), so overfitting is no longer the diagnosable cause and re-issuing it would buy nothing. What is left is the ranking: roc_auc 0.9914 vs 0.9912, and balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut 0.9589 vs 0.9585 — the two families tried span 0.0004, while even at the best possible cut the bar is still 0.0025 away, i.e. the shortfall is ~6x the span the family swap has covered. In KS terms the bar needs 0.9228 and the best ranking so far is 0.9178. cut_headroom 0.0072 against 0.0097 to go means the operating point can supply at most 74% and the last 26% must come from the ranking; recall 0.9392 is below specificity 0.9642, so if a weight lever is spent it must move toward more positive-class weight, not less. No dropped_hyperparams, no error type, train_time 4.2 s of 600 s — resources are not the issue. With 3 iterations left and gbdt-family ranking flat across two members, the honest read is that another point in the same boosted-tree space cannot reach the bar.
critic.direction: Leave the boosting family and try the one structurally different ranking generator on the list — a bagged, fully-grown random_forest (an averaged, high-variance-base ensemble rather than a sequentially-fitted shrunken one) with the pipeline held exactly as before, and spend the same attempt's operating-point headroom by pushing the positive class up, since recall 0.9392 < specificity 0.9642 and cut_headroom 0.0072 covers 74% of the remaining 0.0097 while the other 26% needs the different ranking.

critic.evidence: Iteration 3 (random_forest, 1200 trees, min_samples_leaf 1, class_weight {0:1,1:1.35}) scored balanced_accuracy 0.9545 against the 0.9614 bar — 0.0069 short — with 95% CI 0.9400~0.9681, which contains the bar and both prior attempts (0.9534, 0.9517); the paired Δ vs iteration 1 is +0.0010 (CI -0.0078~+0.0113, P(better) 0.610), so the family swap produced movement this slice cannot resolve from zero. Two things did resolve. First, the operating point is now spent: cut_headroom collapsed from 0.0072 (iter 2) to 0.000145, and recall 0.9448 now equals specificity 0.9642 to within a hair — the 1.35 weight did exactly what I prescribed and landed the cut essentially at its optimum, so at most 2% of the remaining 0.0069 is buyable with any weight or threshold and 98% is in the ranking. Second, the bagged ranking did not beat boosting: roc_auc fell 0.9914→0.9892 and balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut fell 0.9589→0.9546, and the three families tried span only 0.9546~0.9589 (0.0043) at best cut while the bar still sits 0.0025 above the best of them (KS 0.9178 vs required 0.9228). That span is a range over per-family maxima, not a paired test, so it is not evidence the families differ — it is a measure of how little three swaps off this list have bought, and a fourth (extra_trees is a near-neighbour of the forest just tried) is not a plan that reaches the bar. Overfitting is not re-diagnosable as the cause of the shortfall — it paid nothing at iteration 1 and validation has never moved outside its interval — but the forest's train_balanced_accuracy 1.0000 / train_val_gap 0.0456 with calibration_error worsening 0.0156→0.0524 and brier 0.0340→0.0392 says this particular ranking generator is the weaker one and should not be tuned further. No dropped_hyperparams, no error_type, train_time 5.58 s of 600 s: resources are not the issue. With 2 iterations left, the only lever that has never been touched in three attempts is the feature matrix itself — every attempt ran the identical median-impute, no-scaling, no-missingness pipeline.
critic.direction: Go back to the best-ranking family (hist_gbdt, roc_auc 0.9912 / best-cut 0.9585) and change the one thing no attempt has changed — the input columns — by running it with impute: none so the trees split on NaN natively plus missing_count, keeping class_weight at the crossing point the forest just located, because cut_headroom 0.0001 says 98% of the remaining 0.0069 must come from a ranking that a fourth family off the same 0.0043-wide list will not supply.

critic.evidence: Iteration 4 (svc, RBF, C=10, class_weight {0:1,1:1.15}, scale ON) scored balanced_accuracy 0.9337 against the 0.9614 bar — 0.0277 short — with 95% CI 0.9179~0.9500, which for the first time in this run does NOT contain the bar and does not contain iteration 3's 0.9545; the paired Δ vs iteration 3 is -0.0207 (CI -0.0352~-0.0067, P(better) 0.003), so this is a resolved regression. Two levers moved on that row (family kernel→svc AND scale false→true), so the -0.0207 has two owners and cannot be attributed to either; what it does establish is that this kernel point is not the ranking generator the bar needs. The ledger is now decisive on family swapping: four families tried (hist_gbdt 0.9534, xgboost 0.9517, random_forest 0.9545, svc 0.9337), the three trees' balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut spans only 0.9546~0.9589 (width 0.0043) while the bar sits 0.0025 above the best of them even at a perfect cut (required KS 0.9228 vs best 0.9178), and cut_headroom at the best attempt is 0.000145, i.e. ≤2% of the remaining 0.0069 is buyable with any weight. So with one iteration left the honest read is not "try a fifth family off the same list" — it is to return to the single best-ranking generator measured (hist_gbdt, roc_auc 0.9912, best-cut 0.9585) and change the only lever this history has never attributed anything to.
